The members of the Indian Society of Technical Education (ISTE-KJSCE) conducted a seminar on Microsoft Azure on 22nd September 2022. A student of KJSCE, he has made remarkable progress in Cloud Computing and is passionate about mentoring aspiring software engineers.

The seminar was conducted in a friendly yet informative manner, creating an interactive environment. Overall, participants found the session highly insightful and fruitful.

## ABHIYANKTRIKI 2020: The Bro Code

**ABHIYANKTRIKI 2022: The Bro Code** was a technical coding event conducted as part of **Abhiyantriki**. The competition was open to students from all years and branches, including beginners.

Participants were required to solve problem statements using **BhaiLang**, a toy programming language, and create a flowchart for the given problem. This format encouraged logical thinking and problem-solving skills.

The top three winners were awarded prizes worth ₹7000. The event witnessed great enthusiasm among participants, with teams striving to secure the highest points. Overall, the event was successfully conducted, leaving participants satisfied with the team management and gaining valuable technical insights.

## TECHNOVALLEY 

The members of The Indian Society of Technical Education (ISTE-KJSCE) conducted a national-level flagship event on research paper presentation and Working Model Project Competition on 13th April 2023.

The competition was based on multiple themes which are present-day technologies. The judges of the competition were well-renowned experts in the field of technology. There was a total of 10 registrations of groups for the technical paper presentation and 32 registrations for the working model project competition.

The participants included SVU as well as non-SVU students. The guests present for the event were our respected principal, all department HODs, the Vice Principal, the Associate Dean, the Dean, and the controller of the examination.

All the participants were given a token of appreciation through participation certificates and the winners received cash prizes as well. This event was successfully completed with an interactive environment between the students and the judges. Overall, the participants found it highly fruitful.

eventCardDescription: The CreAIte AI Workshop, hosted by Abhinav Gupta, founder of 100xengineers, attracted a diverse audience of college-level AI enthusiasts eager to delve into the fascinating world of artificial intelligence. The workshop was meticulously designed to cover a range of practical AI applications, making it highly relevant for the attendees. It commenced with an in-depth session on effectively using ChatGPT, providing participants with valuable insights into leveraging this tool for various applications. This session highlighted the potential of AI in creating compelling graphics that can captivate audiences and improve engagement. Next, the focus shifted to the Tome.ai presentation tool, which simplifies the process of creating professional presentations using AI, making it an indispensable resource for students and professionals alike. One of the most intriguing parts of the workshop was the demonstration of voice transformation using rvc.ai. This technology allows for realistic voice modifications, showcasing the versatility and potential of AI in audio applications. Throughout the workshop, Mr. Abhinav Gupta's engaging presentation style made complex AI concepts accessible to all participants, regardless of their prior experience with AI. The event concluded on a high note, with participants leaving with a wealth of practical knowledge and inspiration. They were equipped with new skills and ideas on how to incorporate AI into their projects, whether academic or professional. The CreAIte AI Workshop not only provided valuable technical knowledge but also ignited a passion for AI, encouraging participants to explore and innovate further in this exciting field.

## Prakalpa 2024

ISTE-KJSCE organized Prakalpa on April 3, 2024, a prestigious national-level event held at KJ Somaiya College of Engineering. This event was a significant platform for budding engineers and innovators to showcase their research and technical skills through research paper presentations and Working Model Projects.

The event attracted a diverse group of participants, highlighting the widespread appeal and recognition of Prakalpa in the engineering community. The research paper presentation segment featured 26 groups who meticulously presented their findings and innovations to a panel of esteemed judges. These judges, with their extensive expertise and experience, evaluated the presentations based on various criteria including originality, technical depth, clarity of presentation, and the potential impact of the research. This provided a valuable opportunity for participants to gain feedback and insights from experts, helping them refine their research further.

In the Working Model Project Competition, 32 groups showcased their innovative projects, demonstrating practical applications of engineering principles and creative problem-solving. Noteworthy projects included VanyaRakshak; a Wireless EV Charging System that promises to revolutionize electric vehicle infrastructure; a Leaf Detection System for agricultural advancements; the Ultra Vision Stick; a Parabolic Trough Collector & many more.

The event culminated in a grand ceremony where certificates ,hampers and cash prizes upto Rs 50,000/- were awarded to the winners.

The session ended with an engaging quiz to test participant's understanding, followed by a Q&A that allowed them to clarify doubts and exchange insights with peers. Organized by ISTE KJSSE, the workshop empowered students with the skills and confidence to use Figma in their projects, promoting creativity and collaboration in design.

eventCardDescription: The TechTangle Challenge, organized by ISTE KJSSE as part of Abhiyantriki 2024 at K J Somaiya School of Engineering, was a dynamic and intellectually stimulating hybrid competition that tested participant's skills in coding, debugging, and hardware. Featuring four unique task zones, the event provided an engaging platform for students to apply their technical knowledge in a competitive yet collaborative environment.
eventMarkdown:
## TechTangle Challenge

The TechTangle Challenge, organized by ISTE KJSSE at K J Somaiya School of Engineering as part of Abhiyantriki 2024, was a hybrid technical competition designed to evaluate proficiency in both software and hardware domains.

The event featured four task zones:

- **Word-up:** A themed crossword followed by writing code or pseudo-code using the discovered words.
- **DevZone:** A Jenga-inspired coding round involving CSS snippets and output-based tasks.
- **Fixit:** A debugging challenge requiring participants to correct faulty code to match expected outputs.
- **Hardware Challenge:** Assembling a functional circuit using components such as Arduino, I2C LCD, IR sensors, and LEDs.

Open to intercollegiate participation, students competed individually or in teams of two. Judging criteria included accuracy, time efficiency, and number of hints used. A registration fee of ₹50 per individual and ₹80 per duo team was charged, with prizes worth ₹5,000 awarded to top performers.

With proper resources provided and a distinguished KJSSE alumnus interacting with participants, the event successfully fostered practical learning, real-time debugging skills, and innovation among future technocrats.

eventCardDescription: ThinkSprint, organized by ISTE KJSSE, was an intellectually stimulating and fast-paced case study competition designed to test participant's critical thinking, creativity, and collaborative problem-solving skills. Simulating real-world business and technological environments, the event challenged teams to analyze complex scenarios, develop innovative yet feasible solutions, and present their ideas under structured time constraints. Through its two-phase format and expert evaluation, ThinkSprint fostered analytical reasoning, interdisciplinary application, and boardroom-level decision-making skills among students.
eventMarkdown:
## ThinkSprint

ThinkSprint, organized by ISTE KJSSE, was a dynamic case study competition aimed at enhancing critical thinking, creativity, and collaborative problem-solving skills. The event simulated real-world business and technological challenges, encouraging rapid analysis and structured reasoning.

Participants formed teams and tackled complex scenarios across domains such as technology, entrepreneurship, societal challenges, and business strategy. The competition was conducted in two phases. In the first round, teams submitted a proposal outlining their approach, judged on originality, clarity, and potential impact. Shortlisted teams advanced to the final round to present their refined ideas before a panel of expert judges.

The final round was evaluated based on innovation, feasibility, depth of understanding, practicality, and presentation skills. It was judged by Mr. Rajvardhan Patil, an alumnus of KJSSE, who provided valuable industry-oriented feedback and insights.

Registration was free to ensure inclusivity, and winning teams were awarded certificates and cash prizes up to Rs. 10,000. The event successfully promoted analytical thinking, leadership, adaptability, and innovation among participants.

## Prakalpa 2025

The Indian Society for Technical Education (ISTE KJSSE) successfully organized its National Level flagship event, **Prakalpa 2025**, on April 9, 2025, at K J Somaiya School of Engineering. The event featured a Research Paper Presentation and a Working Model Project Competition, providing students a national platform to showcase innovative hardware and software solutions while promoting creativity, research, and technological advancement.

A total of **58 teams** participated, including **39 Working Model projects** (22 hardware and 17 software) and **19 Research Paper presentations**. Participants represented SVU and various institutions across India, with the event marking a milestone by hosting its first international participant.

The event commenced with a traditional lamp-lighting ceremony graced by Director Dr. S. K. Ukarande, Deputy Director Dr. Deepak Sharma, Faculty Advisors Dr. Sushma Kadge and Prof. Abhishek Bhadauria, along with the panel of judges. Dr. Ukarande delivered the inaugural address emphasizing student-led innovation, followed by encouraging messages from Dr. Sharma and Dr. Kadge.

Projects were evaluated by a distinguished panel of judges on parameters such as innovation, feasibility, and impact. Themes included Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, IoT, Cybersecurity, Game Development, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems.

Standout projects included *FireWatch 700: IoT-Based Firefighting Bot*, *Portable Vehicular Emission Detector with Location Tracker*, *Parity Protocol: a Decentralized Compute Network*, and *ColorViTAN: a Vision Transformer-based greyscale image colorization model*.

Participants engaged in insightful discussions with judges and received constructive feedback. All teams were awarded certificates, while winners received cash prizes and goodies. The event also featured a visit from a KJSSE alumnus who inspired participants with professional insights.

Prakalpa 2025 concluded successfully, reaffirming ISTE KJSSE's commitment to fostering innovation, interdisciplinary collaboration, and practical problem-solving among future engineers.

eventCardDescription: Pixel Wars was a fast-paced Game Development Challenge where participants used the GDevelop platform to design and build a simple game within a limited timeframe. The event encouraged creativity, teamwork, rapid prototyping, and problem-solving in a competitive yet collaborative environment, without requiring advanced programming skills.
eventMarkdown:
## Pixel Wars

Pixel Wars was a quick game creation challenge where participants designed and built a simple game using the **GDevelop** platform within a set time. The event emphasized creativity, game mechanics, and rapid prototyping, while requiring minimal coding skills.

### Game Development Challenge
The event began with an inauguration session outlining rules and guidelines. Each team member was assigned an individual system to develop their project. AI tools were prohibited to ensure originality, though participants could use the internet for research and ideation. Predefined assets were provided, and teams were encouraged to create custom assets using Canva or Figma to enhance creativity.

### Participation and Event Management
Open to intercollegiate participants, the event fostered collaboration and healthy competition. Conducted in fully equipped computer labs, personal laptops were not allowed to maintain fairness. Teams registered in pairs, with a fee of ₹50 per duo and ₹80 per squad.

The four-hour challenge included a short break and refreshments, ensuring participants remained energized while building innovative and engaging games.
